quests.sentence: I will definitely finish this important project by next Friday.
quests.hint: 'Will' is followed directly by the base verb to make a prediction or promise.
quests.explanation: Will finish expresses a future prediction or promise, using will plus the base form of the verb.

quests.sentence: She will probably return your important phone call this afternoon.
quests.hint: The adverb 'probably' fits between will and the base verb to show likelihood.
quests.explanation: Will probably return shows a likely future action, with probably placed between will and the base verb.

quests.sentence: The stormy weather will finally improve significantly by this weekend.
quests.hint: Manner adverbs like 'significantly' come right after the main verb.
quests.explanation: Will finally improve significantly shows a future prediction, with the adverb placed after the verb improve.

quests.sentence: I honestly think it will rain again later this evening.
quests.hint: Use 'will' for predictions based on opinion, followed by the base verb.
quests.explanation: Will rain expresses a prediction based on opinion, following the pattern will + base verb.

quests.sentence: We are definitely going to renovate our kitchen next month.
quests.hint: 'Going to' shows a decided plan, unlike 'will' for spontaneous predictions.
quests.explanation: Are going to renovate shows a plan already decided, using be + going to + base verb.

quests.sentence: I will gladly help you carry those heavy boxes upstairs.
quests.hint: 'Will' expresses a decision made at the moment of speaking, like an offer.
quests.explanation: Will gladly help shows a spontaneous offer, using will plus the base verb for an instant decision.

quests.sentence: All airline passengers must fasten their seatbelts before every takeoff.
quests.hint: 'Must' is followed directly by the base verb to show a strict rule.
quests.explanation: Must fasten expresses a strong obligation or rule, using must plus the base form of the verb.

quests.sentence: All employees have to submit their timesheets every single Friday.
quests.hint: 'Have to' functions like 'must' and is followed by the base verb.
quests.explanation: Have to submit expresses an external requirement, using have to plus the base form of the verb.

quests.sentence: You must renew your expired passport before the upcoming trip.
quests.hint: 'Must' is followed by the base verb, then the object and reason.
quests.explanation: Must renew shows a necessary action, using must plus the base verb renew before the time clause.

quests.sentence: You should really drink more water throughout the entire day.
quests.hint: 'Should' is followed directly by the base verb to give advice.
quests.explanation: Should drink gives advice, using should plus the base form of the verb drink.

quests.sentence: All factory workers should report any serious safety concerns immediately.
quests.hint: 'Should' gives strong advice, followed by the base verb report.
quests.explanation: Should report gives recommended advice, using should plus the base verb, followed by the object.

quests.sentence: He really ought to see a specialist about his knee.
quests.hint: 'Ought to' works like 'should' and is followed by the base verb.
quests.explanation: Ought to see gives strong advice, similar in meaning to should, followed by the base verb see.

quests.sentence: We finally arrived safely at the hotel late last night.
quests.hint: The usual order is manner, then place, then time: safely, at the hotel, last night.
quests.explanation: Adverbials typically follow manner + place + time order: safely (manner), at the hotel (place), last night (time).

quests.sentence: She spoke very confidently to the entire crowd yesterday afternoon.
quests.hint: Manner comes first (confidently), then place (to the crowd), then time (yesterday afternoon).
quests.explanation: This sentence follows manner + place + time order: confidently, to the entire crowd, yesterday afternoon.

quests.sentence: They worked tirelessly in the shared community garden all weekend.
quests.hint: Keep the manner adverb right after the verb, then the place, then the time.
quests.explanation: Worked tirelessly (manner) is followed by in the shared community garden (place) and all weekend (time).

quests.sentence: Please remember to turn off your phone during the meeting.
quests.hint: Separable phrasal verbs like 'turn off' can have the object between or after the two parts.
quests.explanation: Turn off your phone keeps the phrasal verb together before the full noun object, a valid separable pattern.

quests.sentence: She picked her young daughter up from school again today.
quests.hint: With separable phrasal verbs, a noun object can go between the verb and the particle.
quests.explanation: Picked her daughter up splits the phrasal verb pick up, placing the noun object between the two parts.

quests.sentence: He carefully filled out the entire application form this morning.
quests.hint: 'Filled out' stays together before a long noun object like a form.
quests.explanation: Filled out the form keeps the phrasal verb together since the object entire application form is quite long.

quests.sentence: Regular daily exercise will greatly improve your overall physical health.
quests.hint: The adverb 'greatly' fits between will and the base verb improve.
quests.explanation: Will greatly improve shows a confident prediction, with greatly placed between will and the base verb.

quests.sentence: Scientists believe the new policy will reduce city pollution significantly.
quests.hint: Manner adverbs like 'significantly' usually come at the end of the sentence.
quests.explanation: Will reduce pollution significantly shows a predicted outcome, with the adverb significantly placed at the end.

quests.sentence: This new law will finally protect the local wildlife better.
quests.hint: 'Will' is followed directly by the base verb protect.
quests.explanation: Will finally protect expresses a confident future prediction, using will plus the base form of the verb.

quests.sentence: Everyone in this city must recycle their plastic bottles carefully.
quests.hint: 'Must' shows a firm rule, followed directly by the base verb.
quests.explanation: Must recycle expresses a required action for everyone, using must plus the base verb recycle.

quests.sentence: Local residents have to separate their household waste every week.
quests.hint: 'Have to' functions like 'must', followed by the base verb separate.
quests.explanation: Have to separate expresses a necessary action, using have to plus the base verb, followed by the frequency phrase.

quests.sentence: All local factories must reduce their carbon emissions this decade.
quests.hint: 'Must' is followed by the base verb reduce, then the object.
quests.explanation: Must reduce shows an urgent requirement, using must plus the base verb, followed by the object and time phrase.

quests.sentence: The busy manager called off the entire meeting this morning.
quests.hint: 'Called off' can stay together before a long noun object like a meeting.
quests.explanation: Called off the meeting keeps the phrasal verb together since the object the entire meeting is fairly long.

quests.sentence: We really need to sort this whole problem out quickly.
quests.hint: With a pronoun-like short object, the particle 'out' often comes after it.
quests.explanation: Sort this problem out splits the phrasal verb sort out, placing the object between the verb and the particle.

quests.sentence: Community volunteers handed the free flyers out around downtown today.
quests.hint: 'Handed out' can split around the object, placing it between the two parts.
quests.explanation: Handed the flyers out splits the phrasal verb hand out, with the object between the verb and the particle.

quests.sentence: I will definitely finish this whole report by Friday morning.
quests.hint: Combine the future tense will with an adverb and a time expression.
quests.explanation: This review sentence mixes future simple (will finish) with an adverb and a closing time phrase.

quests.sentence: All office employees must turn off their computers every night.
quests.hint: Combine the modal 'must' with a phrasal verb and a frequency phrase.
quests.explanation: This checkpoint sentence mixes modal necessity (must turn off) with a phrasal verb and a frequency phrase.

quests.sentence: We finally arrived safely at the busy airport this morning.
quests.hint: Combine the manner adverb, the place phrase, and the time phrase in order.
quests.explanation: This review sentence brings together manner, place, and time adverbials in the standard order.
